_about: Iorez (161171, impostor_priest): translated from the game's Japanese. Terse ex-assassin; 面倒だ is kept as "What a pain". Global names/terms: Nimbus, Light, Alk, Quade Arsalett, Ernest, Palpebra, the Farlands, the Star Augurs, Starview Village. ホロウ = "Hollow", ファトマ教 = the Church of Farlana.
profile: A self-proclaimed priest who serves as a grave keeper in Palpebra. A man of few words who hates anything troublesome. Orders, restraints, even thinking—to him, it's all a pain. The first thing he ever truly wanted was the peace he found in Palpebra.
titleCondition: Level Iorez to 100 and obtain his Amity Scroll

speech.home/hitowakorosanai: I don't kill people. That doesn't mean I can hit people who break the rules, either... Being a regular citizen is a pain.
speech.home/anatanihoshino: May the stars' -- ...blessing... profit...? ......May the stars guide you, was it. Memorizing every little thing is a pain...
speech.home/honwa_kiraijanai: I don't dislike books. They show me worlds I don't know. Understanding and empathy, or whatever they're called, are hard, though.
speech.home/hakamorino: I still keep up my work as a grave keeper. A regular citizen needs a public job, after all. ...The repairs are still a pain, though.
speech.home/anochohatsuno: That long-haired man says he doesn't think like a regular citizen either. ...To me, you all look the same. Strange bunch...
speech.home/oredatte: Even I remember people's names. You're Alk. You're Nimbus. ......I think.
speech.ally/join: ...What a pain... Iorez. Priest and grave keeper. "May the stars guide you." ...Did I say that right?
speech.ally/evolution: Orders and restraints are a pain. ...But if you need my strength, I'll lend it. That's what friends do, isn't it?

1.title: The False Priest Wants Peace
1.summary: Alk and the others take on a request to look into a man called "Iorez", said to be an assassin active in the Farlands. But the man himself has already retired from assassination. Iorez, whose common sense is a bit off, wants to become a regular citizen so he can live in peace, leaving Alk and the others baffled.

lines.5: ...Thank you so much, Nimbus...! Thanks to you I hit every sale! I got everything! I have no regrets...!
lines.9: Nah, carrying bags is no big deal, but... Your eyes sure light up over the weirdest stuff...
lines.26: ...Was that someone from the Church of Farlana? But somehow...
lines.30: He walks way too quietly. And that smell clinging to him--
lines.36: His name is Iorez. It seems he recently became the grave keeper of Palpebra's cemetery.
lines.40: ...That's not how you talk about someone you know, is it?
lines.44: I'd like to look into his background a bit. ...Would you be willing to help?
lines.50: You're there, aren't you? What do you want with me?
lines.54: ...We took a request from the Guild. I used my connections to look into you.
lines.56: A member of a criminal group that specializes in assassination. Active in the Farlands. ...And Iorez is an alias, isn't it?
lines.59: Why did you hide who you are and become a grave keeper? If you plan to do something in Palpebra...
lines.62: There's no need to worry about that. Just hand him over to us.
lines.66: ...You smell alike. One of his buddies?
lines.69: Think what you like. Hand that man over and we'll leave.
lines.70: You want the danger gone. We'd rather not cause a scene in public. ...I'd say our interests align, wouldn't you?
lines.73: Just a family squabble...? ...What do we do?
lines.77: ...Nobody told us to take him into custody, but--
lines.94: Ngh... You traitor...! Pulling a stunt like this...!
lines.106: W-well... There's no need to go that far...
lines.113: This town has no need for something like him. Why let him live?
lines.120: ...Because I don't want to choose that. That's all.
lines.132: An assassin posing as a priest, chased by others in his trade. Something serious must have...?
lines.140: I want to become a regular citizen.
lines.149: So, um... You really did belong to one of the criminal organizations active in the Farlands, Iorez.
lines.153: Yeah. I don't remember dealing with those Star Augurs you mentioned, though.
lines.157: ...But you have no intention of going back to the organization, and would rather not be involved at all...?
lines.161: ...Orders, restraints... I'm done. They're a pain.
lines.163: If I become a regular citizen of this town... of the public world, I can live in peace, right? So I want to become a regular citizen.
lines.167: ...Let me confirm once more. You've washed your hands of that underground work. You can say that?
lines.171: I can. I got a request to assassinate a Guild executive in Palpebra, but I ignored it.
lines.176: You're getting chased like crazy because you ignored it...
lines.184: Don't tell me this guy's the type who's bad at thinking things through?
lines.194: ...I've reported you to the client. It seems the Guild will keep you under watch for a while.
lines.196: They said it's still hard to trust you. ...Earlier, if Alk hadn't stopped you, you wouldn't have hesitated, would you?
lines.203: If I don't kill people, can we become friends?
lines.212: Regular citizens make these things called friends, don't they?
lines.217: W-well, that might depend on the person... But most people do...?
lines.221: Understood. I won't kill people anymore.
lines.224: I'll do what I can to become a friend. A regular citizen. ......Even though it's a pain.
lines.233: So, from now on, I'd like to stay involved with you-- ...to request contact...
lines.235: ...What's the proper thing to say at a time like this?
lines.245: I see. ...I look forward to working with you.

2.title: A Certain Peaceful Day
2.summary: While spending time with Iorez, whose off-kilter common sense keeps dragging him into trouble, Alk and the others learn what made him decide to become a regular citizen. Realizing that Iorez simply wanted to be their friend, Alk and the others show him to Starview Village.

lines.4: And so, from now on, do not call yourself a priest as you please! Never again shall you mock the Church of Farlana--
lines.7: ...Fine. I won't say the star-whatever anymore.
lines.10: Were you even listening!? And "whatever"!? The sheer disrespect!!?
lines.18: Oh, it's you. ...What was the problem just now?
lines.31: Hey, I bet stuff like that isn't rare for you, huh?
lines.35: ...I get complaints a lot. I thought I was keeping things peaceful...
lines.38: Watch me for a while. Tell me what the problem is.
lines.44: A grave keeper's job is to manage and watch over the cemetery. ...I figured patrolling was something even I could do.
lines.48: ...Did you call yourself a priest because it seemed to suit a grave keeper, too?
lines.52: ...That, and it seemed like an easy way to blend in as a regular citizen. Apparently not.
lines.57: What we're saying is your direction and your disguise are both sloppy--
lines.62: Heeey. What are you guys doing?
lines.66: Ah, n-no, nothing! We just kinda got lost! W-we'll head home right a--
lines.73: Um!!? You're pushing peace away all by yourself, aren't you!?
lines.78: As long as I don't kill them, it's fine, isn't it?
lines.83: They obviously weren't hostile... You're just making more work for yourself.
lines.87: ...If I were a regular citizen, what would I normally do after this?
lines.92: Uh... I-I guess fix whatever got broken... maybe?
lines.97: I'll treat your injuries later. Stay here. Don't move.
lines.100: Fixing the gravestone and the fence... More of a pain, all right...
lines.105: Is he lazy or just honest...?
lines.115: ...Don't attack those who aren't hostile. Even when they are, whether to fight back immediately needs consideration...
lines.117: Regular citizens deal with nothing but pains...
lines.121: "Just hit them first" really is his baseline, huh...
lines.126: Hey, do you seriously want to become one? A peaceful regular citizen?
lines.128: You say you want to, but the way you do things doesn't mesh with this town. That's a fact, right?
lines.132: Oh, Iorez? Do you two know each other?
lines.136: Huh, Ernest? Wait, do you two know each other...?
lines.143: When I first came to this town, he spoke to me. Said he was curious about me being alone.
lines.145: And then he handed me an apple. ...I didn't understand why.
lines.149: I got a lot as thanks for a request, so I just shared some, you know? As a "looking forward to knowing you" sort of thing.
lines.157: Ah, no. I have another request after this. It's a shame, but I need to get going.
lines.165: Well then, see you two too. I'd be glad if you let me join in next time.
lines.169: What a smooth talker. Kind of your total opposite.
lines.175: When he gave me that apple, I decided.
lines.177: The organization, taking orders, it was all a pain. But it was all I knew.
lines.179: ...I first came here for an assassination. And I got an apple.
lines.183: I decided to live in this town. To become one of the people here.
lines.192: You said you didn't want to choose to kill people.
lines.195: Just like with that man earlier... I felt like I saw something in you.
lines.197: If I'm going to become a regular citizen, I felt becoming like you all would be best. ...Is that right?
lines.203: You really did just want to be our friend...
lines.207: ......? That's what regular citizens do, isn't it?
lines.212: Well, I guess there's just too much he doesn't know.
lines.217: Yeah. ...Maybe going to all sorts of places would be one way to help?
lines.225: After everything, this guy's no big deal. Let's hit the dining hall for now.
lines.229: Why did you show me this place? ...Isn't it a secret?
lines.234: Who knows. Why don't you figure it out yourself?

3.title: A Very Big Pain
3.summary: Though he calls it a pain, Iorez keeps working at becoming a regular citizen. Then a man from his old organization invites him to join forces. Iorez flatly turns him down, saying he has no interest at all, and puts his strength to use to become a regular citizen like Alk and the others.

lines.8: No matter how much my surroundings or standard of living change, I never want to forget the value of a single G...!
lines.12: ...Money isn't a problem for me. Why go around to grocery stores that are all the same--
lines.17: They're not the same! The first store and the last one have totally different seasonings, and the quality of the meat and fish is--!
lines.26: Keep him company in my place for once. As a regular citizen, yeah?
lines.30: ...But even while you say it's a pain, you actually listen to us pretty well, don't you?
lines.35: ...I don't know what will give me something to think about.
lines.38: To become a regular citizen, there's a lot I have to think about.
lines.40: The answer might be in your words. So I try to listen.
lines.50: Well, sure looks like there's still plenty of trouble around. ...You noticed, right?
lines.57: As a regular citizen, I'll just deal with it myself.
lines.64: ...I don't need that name anymore. And I have no intention of going back to the organization--
lines.67: Hollow, join forces with me. Let's build a new organization.
lines.73: The Farlands are on the verge of upheaval. Now, while the underworld is in chaos, is our chance.
lines.74: We don't need to be bound to our old nest anymore. We'll move the pieces. We'll be the ones doing the binding.
lines.77: ...At times like this... Should I have apologized first?
lines.79: Sorry, but I'm not interested at all. I'm going to be one of this town's people--
lines.82: You, the hollow one? Think you can become "the same" as them?
lines.84: There's no light inside us. No matter how much you imitate them, you'll never become the same.
lines.85: It's just blinding and suffocating. ...You understand that, don't you?
lines.91: The reason to give someone an apple. The wish not to kill people. There's not one bit of it in me--
lines.97: Even so. Even though it was a pain, I thought about it.
lines.99: What it meant that the town welcomed me. Why they smiled. The whole time.
lines.107: Maybe I could have become their friend, don't you think?
lines.110: ...How revolting. I'll bring you back to your senses.
lines.113: ...Don't kill. Don't cause a scene. But I should deal with this fast...
lines.116: ...Wouldn't hitting them be faster after all?
lines.120: ...... Was that the regular citizen's way?
lines.124: Who knows? It's not like we're upstanding or squeaky clean.
lines.128: Hey, sorry. Truth is, we're not exactly regular citizens either.
lines.138: But I'm glad we made it in time. ...Were we butting in?
lines.142: ...It wasn't needed. It was a problem I could have handled myself.
lines.145: But, I see. You come. ...........It's hard...
lines.150: So? What're we doing with these guys?
lines.154: Hand them over to the Guild. ...This might have been good timing.
lines.157: I'll think a little longer. About how to live in this town. My way.
lines.163: Hmm, hmm, hmm~ hmm~ hmm~♪ Now then, where shall we begin?
lines.169: ...I didn't kill them. That's no problem, right?
lines.173: More than enough for a bodyguard. ...But I'm surprised you accepted. I heard you hate orders and restraints.
lines.177: ...I was told to make it a "good relationship". That I don't need to be a pawn.
lines.179: You make good use of my strength and information. The watch on me gets lifted, and I can live more like a regular citizen. ...I thought that wasn't bad.
lines.183: Thanks to you, the investigation really is moving forward. It's true that suspicious new organizations from the Farlands are on the rise.
lines.187: ...And those new organizations are likely connected to the Star Augurs you're chasing-- ...Was that it?
lines.190: If so, cracking down on them gets even more troublesome. Will you still help?
lines.194: The regular citizens I know... Apparently they sometimes do troublesome things for the sake of what they want to choose.
lines.204: Oh, nothing. By the way, keep everything you learn on this job a secret. Pretend you know nothing, like a regular citizen, would you?

1161171/1.19:
A self-proclaimed priest who serves as a grave keeper in Palpebra.
A man of few words who hates anything troublesome.
Orders, restraints, even thinking—to him, it's all a pain.
The first thing he ever truly wanted
was the peace he found in Palpebra.

5000622/1.19:
As the name suggests, this refers to those whose work is managing graves.

In the Farlands, burial according to the widely followed teachings of Farlana is the norm, and nearly all grave keepers who manage the graves are priests of the Church of Farlana.
